Classical result: Kleisli(M) for a strong monad M is always premonoidal; it is MONOIDAL iff M is commutative (in the Power-Robinson sense: the two strength maps agree, cf. nLab 'commutative monad'). CRITICAL disambiguation for MacBeth T1: Power-Robinson commutativity is NOT the same axis as MacBeth's 'non-branching' (arity<=1). Counterexamples found both ways: the powerset monad P is commutative (nLab) yet maximally branching (arity=unbounded); the writer monad Mx(-) for a NON-commutative monoid M is non-branching (arity=1, one output slot) yet NOT commutative in the Power-Robinson sense; the exception monad E+(-) is non-branching (arity<=1) for every E, yet is Power-Robinson-commutative only when |E|<=1. So 'commutative' and 'non-branching' are genuinely orthogonal conditions -- commutativity is neither necessary nor sufficient for MacBeth's arrow-category result. This is a clean negative finding: Power-Robinson commutativity is NOT the classical name for MacBeth's condition; 'non-branching'/'arity<=1 polynomial monad E+Ax(-)' appears to be a genuinely different, more specific classification not already named in this literature (candidate names to search next: 'output monad', 'linear monad', Manes' monad theory).
